_note: Each diagram in the Claude Doc is a widget. Publishing exports its picture to figures/<slug>.png with a screenshot read and records the widget's publish number as 'pub'. 'mermaid_pub' is the publish that diagrams/<slug>.mmd was last checked against; 'rfcsync.py stale' lists any that differ. 'caption' is the embed's caption in the doc: it maps each placeholder of the export to its slug, so a reworded caption keeps its files.

the-whole-design-1-key-1-kind-of-token.caption: Figure 4.1. The whole design: one account key, one kind of token, a database and a blob store

the-chain-of-joins.caption: Figure 5.1. The chain of joins: who can read at each join point, and what sets each hop's guarantee

where-the-account-key-lives-2-places-in-.caption: Figure 5.2. Where the account key lives in the clear, and where only locked copies exist

two-ways-to-collect.caption: Figure 5.3. Two ways to collect: the desktop node and the hosted bridge write into one mirror

create-4-parties.caption: Figure 5.4. Create: the desktop makes the account key and uploads only a locked copy

read-3-parties.caption: Figure 5.5. Read: a token opens its copy of the account key for one request

update-4-parties.caption: Figure 5.6. Update: a new reader or writer gets its own token and its own locked copy

expire-3-parties.caption: Figure 5.7. Expire: an expired token is refused and its copy is deleted

delete-4-parties.caption: Figure 5.8. Delete: access ends when a token's hash and its copy are deleted

unlocking-the-hosted-bridge.caption: Figure 5.9. Unlocking the hosted bridge: the user's device checks the image, then seals the bridge key under a lease

collect-and-push-4-parties.caption: Figure 5.10. Collect and push: messages are encrypted on the collector node before upload

writing-through-the-hosted-bridge.caption: Figure 5.11. Writing through the hosted bridge: each message is sealed to the account's public key

approve-a-reader-or-writer-4-parties.caption: Figure 5.12. Approve a reader or writer: one approval, one token, one locked copy

search-and-retrieve-3-parties-one-reques.caption: Figure 5.13. Search and retrieve: the account key is opened for one request only

update-4-parties-2.caption: Figure 5.14. Update: a writer's change is encrypted on the server inside its request

revoke-and-recover-4-parties.caption: Figure 5.15. Revoke and recover: one deletion cuts a holder off, and recovery needs another approved device

model-outputs-stay-encrypted.caption: Figure 5.16. Model outputs: stored as encrypted writes, delivered as a pointer unless the user chooses full text

latency-budget-targets-at-the-95th-perce.caption: Figure 6.1. Latency budget: targets at the 95th percentile, not measurements

shared-vs-dedicated-3-users.caption: Figure A.1. One shared database compared with one database per user
